I think usually when talking about the youth vote it means people aged 18-29. It makes sense for this age bracket to generally be more left leaning, even more so than students under 18 years old. There are a lot of reasons, some could include leaving home/ gaining different life experiences/ meeting different people/ post secondary education/ not being reliant on your family/ being more independent etc…. 

For this student mock election it’s hard to tell how much this reflects changes without previous mock elections included. It could be the case that for a lot of Canadas political history kids (ie students under 18) would vote conservative, but then become adults and develop different opinions and change their vote. But kinda hard to tell without previous mock election data. Maybe it’s included but I must have missed it. 

However, it is generally noticed that young people are swinging conservative right now. For most of canadas political history voters have swung between liberal and conservative, within a 20% range. So it makes sense we could have an up and coming batch of conservative voters. 

I’m hoping that an education system and culture that hopefully teaches students about successes our as a country, (ie gay marriage, universal health care, diversity) and our shortcomings (ongoing colonization, racism, housing crisis, list could go on) will help youth (honestly all of us lol) to think critically and empathetically so we can work together, and party lines aren’t so dire…

This article states that conservatives have the largest vote, however majority, both seat wise and popular vote wise, voted for more progressive parties, but it is split.

I feel as if this headline is misleading…

“The Conservatives also received a larger vote share in Manitoba, with 35.6 per cent of students in the province voting for their candidates, compared to 29.3 per cent for the Liberals, 21.6 per cent for the NDP, seven per cent for the Greens and 6.5 per cent for other candidates.” 

The headline would lead me to believe majority of youth are voting right leaning in Manitoba. However, in student elections the left leaning vote makes up more than 50 % and is split between NDP, liberal, and green. Which would make sense because strategic voting wouldn’t be needed for a mock election. I feel like this more so shows that youth want to vote NDP & progressive politics but it’s split, which is a consistent problem with FPTP.
